append.vision_ground: Localization also carries a footprint estimate: footprint_center_xyz_m is the centre of the box that bounds the target's measured outline in its own principal frame (z is the median visible height), footprint_extent_m is that box's two sides, longest first, view_tilt_deg is the angle between the camera-to-target ray and straight down, and footprint_view says whether the view was overhead (at most 20 degrees) or oblique. From an oblique camera only the near side is visible, so center_xyz_m, the AABB and the footprint all sit horizontally toward the camera, by up to half the target's depth; an occluding neighbour can also cut the outline short. From an overhead view the outline is the whole top, and the footprint centre is the target's horizontal centre, handles included. An oblique measurement carries overhead_view_pose: a copyable move_pose target that puts the wrist camera 30 cm above the footprint centre looking straight down, with the current jaw yaw; after that move, run this tool again on the wrist camera and use the overhead footprint_center_xyz_m. Placement: measure the receiving surface from overhead before you grasp, while nothing you hold hides it; measure the object from overhead before grasping and, after the close, keep offset = object footprint centre minus the grip-site position; to set the object on the receiver, send the grip site to the receiver's footprint centre minus that offset (horizontal components), holding the yaw. overhead_view_pose is not a reachability or collision check, and the footprint is not ground truth.
